title: Jev state and criteria so a match happens: in_range, idle time, reworded criteria
description: Decision on 21 Sep 2026 after the first live Jev match (sam-l4r.2): both fighters chose 'advance' 99% of the time and stood face to face for a whole round; the rubric said attack is correct 'only when they are in recovery or otherwise cannot block', and nobody ever attacked. Two changes, same five options and same two questions (PRD section 9 unchanged): (1) richer state per fighter: in_range (gap within this character's heavy-slash reach as measured in sam-amj.5 / sam-aug.2: Earthquake A+B lands at gap 160 but whiffs at 60; Nakoruru needs ~45 frames of walking from 160, so about 110 px or less), opponent_idle_frames (action_age while idle), and a can_be_hit style hint; (2) criteria wording rewritten so a fight happens: attack 'when in range and the opponent is not attacking or blocking, or is in recovery', bait 'when both are idle at range', advance 'when out of range', block 'when the opponent is attacking within reach', retreat 'when low on health or the opponent has rage'. Keep the wording identical for both fighters. Verify with a live match: Jev must choose attack at least sometimes and health must change. Owns no PRD section 12 item.
acceptance_criteria: 1) bridge/jev.py builds the state with in_range and opponent_idle_frames and the reworded criteria; unit tests cover the new fields. 2) A live Jev vs Jev run of at least 60 s shows in bridge.log at least three distinct intents applied per fighter including attack, and state health changing for at least one fighter. 3) Notes quote the applied-intent counts and the health outcome.

Changes in bridge/jev.py: state per fighter gains in_range (gap within REACH[char]: Earthquake 80..175 px, Nakoruru 0..110 px, from sam-amj.5/sam-aug.2 measurements), idle_frames (action_age while idle/walking/crouching), attacking, recovering, stunned; the action question's instructions now say rounds are won by landing heavy slashes and standing still gains nothing; criteria reworded (attack default when in_range and the opponent is idle/walking/recovering; advance when not in range; block when the opponent is in startup/active within reach; bait when both idle just outside range; retreat when low with a lead or opponent has full rage and not in range). Same two questions, same five options, identical for both fighters. Tests: test_in_range_and_idle_frames, test_criteria_mention_in_range (26 pass).
Live runs (copies in /tmp/sam2/jev_evidence/): run 2 applied intents p1 {attack 23, advance 21, block 24}, p2 {advance 34, block 8, attack 24}; Nakoruru won round 1 (Earthquake 128 -> 0 in ~35 s). Also added to bridge/core.py: a 'state' log line every 60 frames with the live-gate reason, and exceptions in step() are caught and logged.

title: Replace the dummy with Jev in the bridge: 3 Hz per fighter, parallel, newest wins
description: Wire bridge/jev.py in as the DecisionMaker. Per fighter, a call is issued every 333 ms on its own worker; both fighters run in parallel. The game loop must never wait on a call. The bridge writes the chosen intent to action.json; Lua expands it. Log per call: fighter, seq sent, seq of last applied, round-trip ms, intent, applied or stale, input and output tokens, to /tmp/sam2/bridge.log. notes:
bridge/jevdm.py: JevDecisionMaker with a JevPool per fighter (3 worker threads, each owning one keep-alive JevClient); the bridge's Ticker issues a call every 333 ms per fighter whether or not one is in flight; replies come back through a queue and Applier applies one only if its state_seq is newer than the last applied for that fighter, else counts it stale (tokens counted either way); errors counted. Bridge._step_async wires it (--jev); calls are skipped when a fighter's health is 0 (no round-phase field yet). Telemetry gains a 'jev' block (calls, applied, stale, errors, in_flight, token totals, rtt last/p50) and last_decision carries confidence/probabilities/opponent_recovering. Tests: bridge/tests/test_jevdm.py (newest-wins incl. out-of-order replies with a slow fake client) - 24 tests pass.

Both fighters walked together and stood pressed chest to chest for the whole round; timer ran to 0 with both at full health. The contest is 'correct' under the current rubric (attack criterion: 'Correct only when they are in recovery or otherwise cannot block'; both idle, neither ever recovers because neither attacks) but it is a dead demo. Levers, in order of how little they change the contract: (1) state: add explicit in_range / gap_in_reach fields and the opponent's idle time; (2) criteria wording within the same five options (e.g. attack 'when in range and the opponent is not attacking', bait 'when both are idle at range'); (3) the executor's attack/bait behaviour (sam-amj.1) will not fix this because the intent never arrives. Print candidate addresses with old and new values to /tmp/sam2/ramsearch.txt. Note whether 8-bit or 16-bit reads are used. It must run alongside lua/start_match.lua so searches happen inside a live Earthquake vs Nakoruru match.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/ramsearch.txt shows at least one snapshot-diff run with candidate addresses, old and new values, taken during a live match. 2) lua/ramsearch.lua is committed and its filter modes are listed in notes.
notes: lua/ramsearch.lua: RS.new{base,size,width=8|16,log}; :snapshot(label) via space:read_range(base, end, 8) (one call, 65536 bytes in ~2 ms); :filter(mode, ...) with modes changed, unchanged, increased, decreased, equal v, delta n, between lo hi (compares the last two snapshots over the current candidate set; ~15 ms per 32k candidates); :count(); :values(off) history; :report(path, limit) writes 'addr  v1 v2 v3...' per candidate; :reset(). 16-bit values decoded big-endian; RS.selftest() confirmed read_range bytes == read_u8 and BE decode == read_u16 at 0x100000 (log line 'selftest ... match'). Runner lua/ramsearch_run.lua embeds start_match: idle1/idle2 snapshots -> unchanged (32716 of 32768 words); P1 walks right 60 frames -> changed (98 words / 133 bytes); idle3 -> unchanged (17 words / 36 bytes). Log + report: /tmp/sam2/ramsearch.txt (copy in /tmp/sam2/ramsearch_evidence/). Lead for sam-aug.2: 0x100A7E went 0x0140 -> 0x0179 during the walk and was stable before/after; 0x10104A/0x10108A/0x10108C moved by +2..+4 (camera/scroll?).
close_reason:
criterion 1: /tmp/sam2/ramsearch.txt shows a snapshot-diff run with candidate addresses and old/new values during a live match — evidence: file /tmp/sam2/ramsearch.txt: filter lines ('w16 filter changed -> 98 candidates (from 32716)', 'w16 filter unchanged -> 17 candidates (from 98)') and the appended report with lines like '0x100A7E  0140 0140 0179' (idle2, walked, idle3), taken at frames 1944-2144 of a live Earthquake vs Nakoruru match started by start_match.lua.
criterion 2: lua/ramsearch.lua committed and filter modes listed in notes — evidence: git commit 'Lua RAM diff-search harness over Neo Geo work RAM (sam-aug.1)'; notes list changed, unchanged, increased, decreased, equal, delta, between and the selftest result.

title: Lua holds P1 Right during a fight and the character walks right
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "set_value() moves a character in this game". Extend the Epic 1 script into lua/walk_right.lua: after coin and start, press P1 A (port :edge:joy:JOY1 field "P1 A") to accept the default character, wait a fixed number of frames for the round to begin, then hold field "P1 Right" for ~120 frames and release. Log the frame ranges to /tmp/sam2/walk_right.txt. Timing may be done with frame counts only; no memory reads yet. Record in notes whether set_value() on a digital field needs 1/0 or the field mask, and whether the value persists between frames or must be reasserted every frame.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen that the P1 character walks to the right for roughly two seconds during round 1 with no keyboard input. 2) /tmp/sam2/walk_right.txt shows the frame range in which P1 Right was held. 3) Notes state the verification result for the section 12 item and the set_value() value semantics found.
notes:
set_value semantics (observed): field:set_value(1) on a digital field asserts the input and the override PERSISTS across frames until field:clear_value(); one set at frame 1000 and one clear at 4000 produced continuous walking. Value is compared to zero (docs), so 1 is enough; no mask needed.
Run 1 (lua/walk_right.lua v1, hold 660-1560): P1 A at frame 540 (2 s after Start) was ignored by the select grid; held Right moved the SELECT CURSOR to the right (snap 0002 vs 0005); the grid auto-picked at ~frame 1250 (~13 s after it appeared); story intro followed; hold window ended before the fight. Finding for sam-g6e.1: the select cursor responds to held directions; confirm needs A later than 2 s after Start.
Run 2 (v2: A at 720 confirms, A taps at 1200/1500 skip story text, Right held 1000-4000, snapshots every 240 frames via manager.machine.video:snapshot() -> ~/mame/snap/samsho2/NNNN.png): 0016 @2440 EN GARDE, P1 (Jubei, default cursor) at left edge; 0017 @2680 P1 mid-screen beside Cham Cham, timer 97; 0018 @2920 stage scrolled, P1 at right edge, timer 91. Copies in /tmp/sam2/walk_evidence/run2/. Round 1 went live at roughly frame 2450-2500 from script start with this sequence.
Environment findings: (1) MAME shows a 'press any button to continue' game-info screen at launch; Zohaib had been pressing it by hand on every run. Fixed by adding -skip_gameinfo to the launch in run-lua and start-app skills. (2) -sound none added to launches (audio distracting; sound is out of scope). (3) MAME does not exit on SIGTERM; stop-app needed SIGKILL both times. Graceful stop should later go through Lua manager.machine:exit().
MAME Lua API confirmed in docs (ref-core): machine:save(filename), machine:load(filename) (for sam-g6e.3), video.speed_percent (for sam-7ij.3 / sam-e8s.5), video:snapshot().
Run 3, fully hands-free (-skip_gameinfo -sound none, no key pressed by anyone): identical frames to run 2 — snap 0029 @2440 EN GARDE P1 left edge, 0031 @2920 P1 right edge, stage scrolled, timer 91. Copies in /tmp/sam2/walk_evidence/run3/. The launch sequence is deterministic across runs. PRD section 12 'set_value() moves a character': VERIFIED.
close_reason:
criterion 1: P1 walks right for ~2 s during round 1 with no keyboard input — evidence: screen snapshots from the hands-free run (no key pressed by anyone, -skip_gameinfo): /tmp/sam2/walk_evidence/run3/0029.png @frame 2440 EN GARDE, P1 at left edge; 0031.png @2920 P1 at right edge, stage scrolled, timer 91 (~8 s of walking). Zohaib did not state a verbal confirmation; he instructed me to close on the evidence and move on (21 Sep). Snapshots were sent to him in chat.
criterion 2: /tmp/sam2/walk_right.txt shows the hold frame range — evidence: file lines 'frame 1000 press P1 Right' and 'frame 4000 release P1 Right', snapshots logged every 240 frames.
criterion 3: notes state the section 12 result and set_value semantics — evidence: bead notes: set_value(1) persists until clear_value(), value compared to zero, no mask needed.
PRD section 12 'set_value() moves a character in this game': VERIFIED — one set_value(1) on P1 Right walked the character across the whole stage.

description: Add a control channel to the bridge (same WebSocket, or a local command file; name the choice) with commands pause, resume, reset, stop.
